title: Parameter contract ledger and recovery guidance for function-call JSON schemas
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: runtime function/tool calling currently lacks a single canonical JSON schema contract format and a clear runtime-compatible migration path. Different callers and model adapters apply inconsistent coercion/strictness rules (unknown fields are sometimes dropped, sometimes cause errors; integer/float coercion varies), making integrations brittle. We need a compact, versioned 'parameter contract ledger' concept: a small, immutable manifest attached to every published function/tool describing parameter schema, coercion policy, compatibility hints, and recommended recovery behaviors. Goals: 1) Define the ledger structure, fields, and versioning conventions. 2) Specify validation semantics (strict vs permissive), coercion rules, and how unknown fields are handled. 3) Provide a standard error taxonomy and human-friendly messages with recovery suggestions. 4) Define runtime behaviors for streaming/partial outputs when a function call requires multi-part parameter collection. 5) Design migration rules and compatibility headers so older clients and servers can negotiate behavior. Deliverables: canonical ledger JSON format, runtime validator spec, SDK helper patterns for authors, and a set of standardized error codes and sample messages for UI/console consumption.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical parameter contract ledger JSON schema is published and documented in the internal PRD.
Runtime validator implements strict and permissive modes with explicit coercion-policy setting (no implicit undocumented coercion).
Error taxonomy with codes (PC_001..PC_099) and suggested recovery steps is available and used by the runtime.
SDK helpers (JS + Python) include: validate(params, ledger), explain(errors), and coerce(params, ledger, policy).
Backward/forward compatibility rules are defined and demonstrated in integration tests covering added/removed fields and type widening (int->float, string->enum).
Console displays contract-version, validation errors, and a one-click suggested fix when possible.
Performance regression <5% on p95 latency for valid calls after validator enabled (bench results attached).
implementation_notes: Ledger fields: id (string), version (semver-like), parameters (array of {name,type,required,default,description}), coercion_policy (strict|permissive|opt-in), compatibility_notes (free text), deprecation_policy (date|version), enum_stability (stable|experimental), examples (array).

Validation semantics: 'strict' rejects unknown fields and type mismatches; 'permissive' will log and attempt coercion if a coercion rule exists. Coercion only allowed when explicitly opted-in in ledger.

Unknown field strategy: ledger can declare unknown_fields: 'reject' | 'ignore' | 'preserve' (preserve passed through to downstream tool). Default is 'reject' for P1 APIs and 'ignore' for legacy-compat endpoints.

Error taxonomy: PC_001 ParameterMissing, PC_002 TypeMismatch, PC_003 EnumViolation, PC_004 UnknownFieldRejected, PC_010 CoercionFailed, PC_020 SchemaVersionConflict. Each error includes 'human_hint' and 'recovery_suggestions'.

Recovery patterns: Suggested actions returned inline (e.g., add missing key, convert string->int, choose from enum). For programmatic recovery include a 'suggested_payload' base64 blob for one-click apply in Console.

Ledger version negotiation: client may send header 'X-Contract-Version: <id>@<version>'. Runtime will attempt to validate against that version; if absent, runtime uses latest stable and returns PC_020 with compatibility hints when mismatch detected.

Streaming/partial collection: ledger may mark parameters as 'streamable'. When a call is split into multiple partial JSON fragments, the runtime will accept 'partial=true' requests and attempt incremental validation; final commit requires full validation. Streaming validation errors are surfaced as non-fatal until commit unless parameter is 'required_immediate'.
Observability: emit metric 'contract.validation.failures' with tags: api, model, contract_id, error_code. Emit a histogram of time-to-fix for suggested fixes applied in Console.
Telemetry and privacy: do not log full parameter values for PII-marked parameter entries; ledger allows parameter-level pii: true|false and runtime must redact in logs and error hints.
SDK helpers will expose explain(errors) that maps PC_* codes to localized human hints and to a repair function when possible.
test_plan: Unit tests for validator rules: required/optional, enum handling, numeric coercion, array item validation.
Integration tests that simulate client with older contract-header and ensure proper PC_020 handling and graceful fallback.
Fuzz tests generating unknown fields and deeply nested payloads to verify rejection thresholds and DoS protections.
Performance benchmarks measuring p50/p95/p99 impact for validated and non-validated paths with 1M request samples from synthetic workload.
Human QA session: ask solutions and SDK teams to author 10 real-world contract ledgers and validate end-to-end behavior.
End-to-end Canary: roll out validator in permissive mode for 48h on a small fraction of traffic with enhanced logging, then flip strict on via rollout policy.
